family: VT-15 Post-maneuver orbit (ML-FR-006 AC5, ML-FR-010 AC3); also VT-12, VT-13
description: Highly elliptical, Molniya-like (conditioning near perigee), ν₀ = 0.0 rad; apsis-tangential burn Δv_RSW = [0.0, 50.0, 0.0] m/s at t_s = 0
status: Committed before any engine run on it (tolerances.md §4.1 item 1). Not yet reviewed or approved; immutable once approved, corrections create a new version (plan §6).

constants.source: WGS 84 values as written in docs/architecture/proposed-architecture.md §3 (ML-ARCH-002); passed explicitly to every Orekit orbit and propagator, Orekit's own constants not used

inputs.requestNote: inputs.requestBody is a SimulationRequest without requestId (contracts-v1.md §4); the consumer adds requestId = "sha256:" + hex(SHA-256(canonicalRequestPayload(body))) (§7) with @mission-lab/contracts. Its initialState is the Orekit element→state of inputs.elements with −0 normalised to +0, and is exactly the state given to Orekit (assumption A4).

model.constantsSource: WGS 84 values as written in docs/architecture/proposed-architecture.md §3 (ML-ARCH-002); passed explicitly to every Orekit orbit and propagator, Orekit's own constants not used
model.units: SI: m, m/s, s, rad, m³/s²
model.time: t_s: elapsed SI seconds from the epoch (contracts-v1.md §2)

producedBy.runtime: Python 3.13.17; JDK 21.0.13 (Eclipse Adoptium, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 21.0.13+9-LTS); Windows 11 AMD64
producedBy.orekitApi: KeplerianPropagator(CartesianOrbit) per segment; LOFType.QSW.rotationFromInertial(PV).applyInverseTo(Δv_RSW) for the inertial Δv; new KeplerianOrbit(PV, GCRF, date, μ) for the elements
producedBy.frameAndTime: Orekit frame FramesFactory.getGCRF() (root of Orekit's frame tree; no transformation applied). Epoch 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z represented in Orekit as 2026-01-01T00:00:00 TAI (UTC needs the leap-second table of orekit-data, not installed; two-body motion depends only on elapsed time, so the label of the origin changes no number); sample date = epoch.shiftedBy(t_s) with the binary64 t_s (tolerances.md §9.3).
producedBy.independence: Generated from Orekit and the contracts only. packages/astrodynamics, packages/simulation, conformance/ and the L2 reference code were not read or run.
producedBy.numberFormat: Every number is the shortest decimal that round-trips to the binary64 value, in the ECMA-262 Number::toString form; JSON.parse restores the exact binary64. −0 is written as {"$number": "-0"} (test-data/reference-cases/README.md encoding); request inputs are normalised to +0 (contracts-v1.md §11.4 P3).

method.rswMapping: Contract RSW (R = r/‖r‖, W = (r × v)/‖r × v‖, S = W × R, pre-maneuver state; contracts-v1.md §2, §3.1) = Orekit LOFType.QSW with Q ↔ R, S ↔ S, W ↔ W, Δv_RSW = [ΔvR, ΔvS, ΔvW] given to Orekit as the local vector (x, y, z) unchanged. The mapping is checked numerically by selfcheck.py (axes vs the contract definitions in binary64, VT-11 bounds). Only the rotation is used (no frame-rate term).
method.impulse: Position unchanged; velocityAfter[k] = velocityBefore[k] + deltaV_inertial[k], one binary64 addition per component (contracts-v1.md R12); deltaV_magnitude = √(Σ Δv_I,k²) in binary64.
method.segments: Segment 0 from the request initial state, segment 1 from the event state (position_m, velocityAfter_mps); first sample of each segment copied from its initial state (contracts-v1.md §5.2 revision 3); sample times per §5.2.
method.elements: Orekit KeplerianOrbit from the event state, angles exactly as Orekit returns them (Orekit's ranges, no normalisation, no ADR-008 convention: for near-circular or near-equatorial states the angles Orekit returns for ω, Ω, ν are not comparable with the engine's convention; compare a, e, i, and the state).

tolerance.record: docs/verification/tolerances.md revision 3: §7 VT-11/VT-12 (frame), VT-13, VT-15 (a⁺, e⁺), §9.3 (states)
tolerance.frame: VT-12: ‖ΔΔv_I‖ ≤ 8(12κ_h + 25)u·‖Δv_RSW‖ (κ_h of the pre-maneuver orbit). Valid against these Δv_I only when the engine's event state equals this one bit-for-bit (maneuver at t_s = 0); for m > 0 the event states differ by propagation error and the comparison must restart from the engine's event state.
tolerance.segment1Note: Segment 1 starts from the Orekit event state. An engine comparison must either restart the reference from the engine's event state (rerun generate.propagate) or add the VT-14 transport term; for a hyperbolic segment no tolerance is evaluated (tolerances.md §7 VT-16: generalised budget per dataset, not derived here; open item O-5).
